name: Licensing Synthetic Media
title: Licensing Synthetic Media
answer: Licensing synthetic media covers the terms under which AI generated images, video, audio and text may be used, sold, remixed or redistributed. It sits inside the wider field of rights and provenance in AI art, where the questions are who owns an output, what the model was trained on, and what a buyer or publisher is actually allowed to do with the file. The subject spans model licences, output terms of service, stock and agency contracts, and the emerging practice of attaching provenance data to a generated asset. It matters to anyone who commissions, publishes, or resells machine made media.

crumbs.name: Rights and Provenance in AI Art

sections.body: Licensing synthetic media covers the terms under which AI generated images, video, audio and text may be used, sold, remixed or redistributed. It sits inside the wider field of rights and provenance in AI art, where the questions are who owns an output, what the model was trained on, and what a buyer or publisher is actually allowed to do with the file. The subject spans model licences, output terms of service, stock and agency contracts, and the emerging practice of attaching provenance data to a generated asset. It matters to anyone who commissions, publishes, or resells machine made media.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: The work runs on the generation platforms themselves and on the metadata systems that travel with their output. This site currently tracks 1,000 live image generation models, 1,000 video models and 2,000 audio models, and each carries its own licence terms, which is why a single asset can arrive with several overlapping sets of conditions. Provenance tooling such as C2PA content credentials and watermarking schemes sit alongside the model, recording how a file was made and what it was made from. Asset management systems, contract repositories and rights databases hold the resulting records so that a licence can be checked later.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: Practitioners read the model licence, the platform terms and the commissioning contract together, because the three often disagree about commercial use, attribution and redistribution. They then record the chain of generation, including prompts, model version, and any reference images supplied, so that the output can be traced back to its inputs. Provenance metadata is embedded or attached at export, and a rights record is filed with the asset. Where a work is registered or disputed, the same record becomes the evidence base, which is why the field leans heavily on documentation rather than on assertion.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Rights and risk here turn on training data, output ownership and disclosure. Courts and registries in several jurisdictions are still working out whether a purely machine generated output attracts copyright at all, and whether training on protected works requires a licence. This site currently tracks 93 active intellectual property lawsuits, of which 18 involve AI music services, which shows how quickly the disputes have moved from images into audio. Platforms increasingly require labels or credentials on synthetic media, and buyers increasingly ask for indemnities. Nothing in this area is settled law, and the practical position differs by country and by contract.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: The direction of travel is toward standardised provenance and clearer licence layering. Content credentials are moving from optional to expected in publishing and advertising workflows, and model providers are beginning to publish training data summaries alongside their terms. Licensing is likely to split into tiers, with separate terms for commercial use, style imitation, and voice or likeness, and collective or blanket licences may emerge for training corpora. Enforcement will depend on whether provenance survives editing and re-upload, which remains the weak point. The disputes now in court will shape the default terms for years.
